desc: Design an O(n) algorithm that computes the max subarray sum after deleting all occurrences of a value x
Prove correctness of the O(n) approach: show it captures the max subarray sum after deleting all x's for any x, and that it's sufficient to consider only negative x's

Recognize that the gap-sums approach has a bug: the formula PS[j] - PS[i-1] + |x|*(j-i) overcounts because the bonus |x|*k should only apply when the subarray spans across x's, not when it includes full gaps. The correct approach is to use the actual stripped array (Kadane on non-x elements) or a proper prefix-based method with the running minimum of P[l] - x*c_x(l-1).
Test edge cases: n=1, all elements same, all negative, mix with zeros

Implement a correct O(n) solution: for each negative x, use the formula f(x) = max_{r: nums[r]!=x} (P[r+1] - x*c_x(r) - min_{l<=r, nums[l]!=x} (P[l] - x*c_x(l-1))), processing in O(k) per x by exploiting the structure of c_x(l-1) as a step function.
Ensure O(n) time and O(n) space, write final solution with comments
Handle edge case: if all elements are negative and equal, cannot delete (array becomes empty), return max single element

Optimize: for x<0, f(x) = Kadane on the array with x's as 0. This is equivalent to running Kadane while skipping x's. Process each distinct negative x in O(n) time. Total O(n * distinct) in worst case, but with n=1e5, this may TLE. Need to find O(n) solution or optimize with early pruning (e.g., only consider x if it appears in a "blocking" position).
